_comment: What each fixture is expected to do when decoded by a RELEASED client's
Swift models. `verify_against_clients.sh` asserts reality matches, so these
are pinned facts rather than notes — if a client change flips any of them,
the script fails and the contract gets revisited.
'fails' means the payload breaks the iOS decode outright, taking the whole
catalog with it. 'tolerated' means it decodes cleanly and the rule exists
for a reason the Swift decoder cannot see — the Android map, or the engine.
Both are legitimate reasons to refuse to publish; only the first is a reason

compliant.why: The baseline. If this ever fails, the contract is too loose and the gate would publish data that bricks the fleet.

violation-missing-limits.why: SpeedLimits.truck/bus are non-optional Int with a synthesized Codable, so an absent key throws keyNotFound and fails the ENTIRE ZonesResponse decode. This is the 2026-08 Път I-8 outage — every published iOS install lost zone sync for five days.

violation-missing-key.why: Any non-optional Zone key behaves the same way; `description` stands in for the class.

violation-short-point.why: Decodes as [[Double]] but the released map layer subscripts point[0]/point[1] unguarded, so a 1-element point traps. The driver reproduces that access rather than only the decode.

violation-empty-centerline.why: Decodes cleanly on iOS. Refused because MapLibre on Android rejects the ENTIRE zone FeatureCollection over one invalid LineString — all 76 zones vanished from the map in 2026-08 while sync reported success. Pinned as tolerated so nobody 'fixes' the Swift check to expect a failure that will never come.

violation-zero-endpoint.why: (0, 0) is a valid Double pair. Refused because the engine can never detect such a zone and map camera fits get dragged toward the Gulf of Guinea.

violation-zero-distance.why: Valid Int. Refused because it divides through the average-speed and remainder math.

violation-zero-limit.why: Valid Int. Refused because a 0 km/h limit reads as permanently over-limit for that vehicle class — which is exactly what Android 1.x's Gson produces when it zero-fills an absent key.
